## Key Drivers

• **Indian banks — FCNR(B) deposit surge and margin/asset-quality concerns** — A record flood of FCNR(B) deposits (reported around $127 billion) left banks scrambling for overseas funding and pushed hedging costs higher, while Axis Bank's CEO warned the inflows could fuel "abnormal lending." This combination of higher funding costs and potential asset-quality risk weighed on the fund's bank holdings, including ICICI Bank, SBI, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Axis Bank, all of which fell during the week.

• **Public-sector bank strike** — Unions announced a nationwide bank strike on 11 September, and SBI itself flagged possible operational disruption. The strike weighed on SBI and added to the broadly negative sentiment toward PSU banks, a meaningful drag given SBI is one of the fund's larger bank positions.

• **Foreign allocation concerns for Indian financials** — Jefferies flagged that foreign investors may rejig allocations away from Indian financials (and highlighted CEO succession concerns), pressuring large private banks including ICICI Bank and Axis Bank. This reinforced the sector-wide selling pressure that drove the fund's financial exposure lower.

• **Rising bond yields** — The India 10-year bond yield crossed 7%, a headwind for financial asset valuations and debt holdings coinciding with the sector's weakest day. This macro move added to the pressure on the fund's finance-related exposure.

• **HDFC Bank — CEO succession update and positive analyst views (offset)** — An update on HDFC Bank's CEO appointment process, along with bullish brokerage commentary, drove a sharp intraday climb and helped the stock gain for the week. As one of the fund's largest holdings, this provided a meaningful partial offset to the broader financials weakness.

## Overall Summary

The fund's decline was driven mainly by its large financials exposure, as Indian banks were hit by a combination of record FCNR(B) deposit inflows, rising hedging and funding costs, an industry warning about abnormal lending, and a public-sector bank strike. Foreign reallocation concerns for Indian financials and the 10-year bond yield crossing 7% compounded the pressure across the fund's bank holdings, including ICICI Bank, SBI, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Axis Bank. A notable explained offset came from HDFC Bank, which rose on a CEO succession update and bullish brokerage views, though this was not enough to offset the broad weakness in financials that shaped the week's negative result.
